column2: A closed loop in 3D space that does not cross itself. Two knots are the same if one deforms into the other without cutting.

column1: Why must the ends of a knotted string be glued?
column2: On an open string every tangle slides off the end. Gluing traps the knot.

column1: What does a knot diagram add to a shadow?
column2: Over/under information at each crossing, drawn as a gap in the under-strand.
R1: add or remove a twist. R2: slide a strand over another (two crossings). R3: slide a strand across a crossing.
Two diagrams show the same knot exactly when a sequence of R1, R2 and R3 moves connects them.
A quantity unchanged by every Reidemeister move. Different values prove different knots. Equal values prove nothing.
Color arcs with 3 colors, at least 2 used. At each crossing the three ends are all one color or all different.

column1: Is the trefoil tricolorable? The unknot? The figure-eight?
column2: Trefoil yes. Unknot no. Figure-eight no.
The fewest crossings over all diagrams of the knot. Trefoil 3, figure-eight 4.
Orient both strands upward. Over-strand heading up-right: \( +1 \). Up-left: \( -1 \). Writhe is the sum of signs.
Half the sum of the signs of the crossings between them. Hopf link: \( \pm 1 \).

column1: What is special about the Borromean rings?
column2: No two rings are linked, yet the three together cannot be separated.

column1: What is a connected sum of knots?
column2: Cut each knot open and join the loose ends with two parallel strands. Every knot is a sum of primes in exactly one way.
The fewest crossing switches that turn the knot into the unknot. Trefoil: 1.
\( \langle \times \rangle = A\langle \text{A-smoothing} \rangle + A^{-1}\langle \text{B-smoothing} \rangle \), each extra loop multiplies by \( -A^2 - A^{-2} \).

column1: Jones polynomial of the trefoil and its mirror?
column2: Left-handed: \( -t^{-4} + t^{-3} + t^{-1} \). Right-handed: \( t + t^3 - t^4 \). They differ: the trefoil is not its own mirror image.
